Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-long-0128", "row_sha256": "df3ac65ac8d350b1de55e76f9e9ed840b248eab3f599bc613c26e05cc417b86f", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
hey, can you help me sort out this bakery order form before i send it to the shop manager? the actual job i want is to reorganize the existing form so a customer can move through it in a sensible order, but only do that if the form already has both a field for the pickup date and a separate field for the pickup time or time window. those are two different things and i don't want one inferred from the other. if either one isn't there, don't reorganize the form; instead give me a concise list saying which of those two fields is missing. that list is the useful alternative because the manager can decide what needs adding before we rearrange anything. return only the applicable result, no intro or explanation around it.

this is for a small neighborhood bakery taking advance orders for the Saturday counter pickup. the form is meant for customers who already know what they want, not a general menu or a marketing page. please keep the scope to the order form itself. i want the sections arranged so the customer information comes before the products, and the pickup information comes after the products. payment details should be easy to find too, but don't move the pickup date into payment or treat the pickup window as a payment detail. keep those two pickup fields separate and plainly labeled. don't turn this into a new checkout system or suggest a new ordering process; the manager just needs a better arrangement of the form we have.

here's the form text as it currently exists, more or less in the order it was copied out of the old document. it starts with “Saturday Bakery Order,” then says orders should be submitted by Thursday at 4 p.m. The customer fields are full name, mobile number, and email address. The item part has columns for product, quantity, and notes, followed by the current products: country sourdough loaf, six cinnamon rolls, lemon tart (eight-inch), and mixed cookie box (12 pieces). the notes column is for things like slicing the loaf or writing a short message on the tart. there isn't a place to ask for a delivery address, because these are counter pickups. please don't add one or imply that delivery is available.

further down in the form there is a field called “Requested pickup date” and another field called “Pickup time window.” the time-window choices are 9:00–10:00 a.m., 10:00–11:00 a.m., and 11:00 a.m.–noon. keep the choices exactly as written and don't turn them into appointment times or promise that an order will be ready at a particular minute. those fields already exist separately, which is why i think they might get missed when the old form is rearranged. checking for both of them is the condition for doing the main task, not a reason to add any pickup details that aren't in the form.

there's also a short payment area and a policy note near the bottom. payment is due at pickup; the accepted methods shown are cash, debit card, and credit card. the policy says, “Please call the bakery before Thursday at 4 p.m. if you need to change an order.” Keep that sentence exactly as it is, including the deadline and the request to call. don't change payment due at pickup to payment in advance, and don't make up a cancellation or refund policy. the ordering deadline appears near the title already, but if you move the surrounding form content, keep the deadline with the form rather than dropping it or changing Thursday to another day.

what i need is the same information put into a clearer sequence, not a redesign of the bakery's wording or an edit to the business rules. keep all four product names, the sizes and counts, the customer field labels, the notes function, the pickup options, payment methods, and the two separate pickup fields. don't add prices, availability claims, allergen statements, a tax line, or a signature field; none of those are part of this form. if you make the main reorganization, use straightforward section headings and keep the order deadline visible. a numbered section is fine if it helps the sequence, but it doesn't need decorative copy.

one thing i heard the manager say was, “people should be able to tell what they need to fill in before they get to the counter.” that's why i want the customer details and requested items grouped rather than scattered around the page. keep the manager's point in mind as the reason for the organization, but don't insert that quote into the customer-facing form. the existing name “Saturday Bakery Order” should stay, and the Saturday pickup context should not be turned into a claim that orders are only accepted on Saturdays; the form says when this batch is for, while the deadline is Thursday at 4 p.m.

if the source i pasted has both a requested pickup date and a separate pickup time-window field, reorganize the form information into a customer-details section, an order-items section, a pickup section, and a payment/policy section, keeping each original fact under the most sensible heading. if it does not have both fields, return only a concise list identifying which one or both are absent, and don't provide a reorganized form in that case. either way, don't add an explanation before or after the result. i only need the relevant output, not a description of what you changed.", "output": "Reorganize the bakery order form below only if it contains both a requested pickup date field and a separate pickup time or time-window field. If either field is absent, do not reorganize the form; return only a concise list identifying which field or fields are missing. Return only the applicable result, with no introduction or explanation.

If both fields are present, arrange the existing information under these sections, in this order:
1. Customer details
2. Order items
3. Pickup
4. Payment and policy

Keep the existing title, “Saturday Bakery Order,” and keep the Thursday at 4 p.m. order deadline visible. Put the customer details before the products, and the pickup information after the products. Keep the requested pickup date and pickup time window as separate, plainly labeled fields. Preserve the time-window choices exactly as written. Do not present them as appointment times or promise readiness at a particular minute.

Preserve the existing customer fields: full name, mobile number, and email address. The order-item table has columns for product, quantity, and notes. The notes are for requests such as slicing the loaf or writing a short message on the tart. Keep all four products and their quantities or sizes exactly as provided: country sourdough loaf; six cinnamon rolls; lemon tart (eight-inch); and mixed cookie box (12 pieces). Do not add a delivery address or imply that delivery is available; these are counter pickups.

In the payment and policy section, retain that payment is due at pickup and that cash, debit card, and credit card are accepted. Preserve this policy sentence exactly: “Please call the bakery before Thursday at 4 p.m. if you need to change an order.” Do not change the payment timing, invent a cancellation or refund policy, or alter the deadline.

Use the same information, arranged in a clearer sequence. Do not redesign the business rules or add prices, availability claims, allergen statements, a tax line, or a signature field. Keep the Saturday pickup context without suggesting that orders are accepted only on Saturdays. Use straightforward section headings; a numbered section is fine. Do not include the manager’s quote in the customer-facing form.

Source form:

Saturday Bakery Order
Orders should be submitted by Thursday at 4 p.m.

Customer fields: full name, mobile number, email address.

Order items — columns: product, quantity, notes. Products: country sourdough loaf; six cinnamon rolls; lemon tart (eight-inch); mixed cookie box (12 pieces). The notes column is for things like slicing the loaf or writing a short message on the tart.

Requested pickup date: [field]
Pickup time window: 9:00–10:00 a.m., 10:00–11:00 a.m., 11:00 a.m.–noon.

Payment: due at pickup. Accepted methods: cash, debit card, credit card.

“Please call the bakery before Thursday at 4 p.m. if you need to change an order.”"}]
